motion.name: scroll-travel-desktop
motion.purpose: User-authorized slower film section height; overrides the global 560vh default for this hero only.

motion.name: scroll-travel-tablet
motion.purpose: User-authorized film section height at widths at or below 1024px (global default 490vh unchanged).

motion.name: scroll-travel-mobile
motion.purpose: User-authorized film section height at widths at or below 768px (global default 420vh unchanged); static mode overrides to auto.

motion.name: lenis-preserved
motion.purpose: Incumbent shared scroll owner; no independent smoothing loop.

motion.name: curtain-spring
motion.purpose: Strand opening spring and pointer smoothing in CurtainLayer; sleeps at rest.

motion.name: curtain-hover-open
motion.purpose: Maximum opening while a fine pointer hovers; scrolling opens fully by 1.3s. No curtain button.

motion.name: curtain-scroll-open
motion.purpose: Film time by which scrolling fully opens the curtain.

motion.name: curtain-end
motion.purpose: Film time after which the curtain and room plate stop drawing and the original film shows.

motion.name: navbar-reveal
motion.purpose: Navbar reveal once Collections enters by 32px; reduced motion removes the transform.

motion.name: scroll-pacing
motion.purpose: User-requested HERO_PACING curve: shorter curtain/opening, longer glass-lettering reveal before 04 Explore.

motion.name: timeline-tip
motion.purpose: Scrub tip (chapter + time) shown only while the rail is hovered, focused or dragged.

scope.surface: Homepage cinematic hero: curtain layer, film overlays, timeline, ending index, static reader, and the navbar's hero-only hide/reveal rule
scope.primitivePolicy: Frontmatter owns primitive tokens. No duplicate token arrays or synthesized tonal scales. Literal values inside standalone preview CSS are render-only transcriptions of the actual components, not a second token registry.
scope.previewPolicy: Control snippets are static visual samples, not executable film navigation. They contain no framework utilities, external icons or media downloads.
scope.verification: Extracted from the current curtain/timeline implementation and its recorded emulated review (headless Chromium, real pointer movement). Actual-phone Safari/Instagram review remains pending. Root design/product files are not modified.

narrative.overview:
The supplied cinematic CGI film leads this homepage hero. The first viewport is artwork: the introduction to Gwee Per Ming and Ming Creatives waits behind an interactive foreground curtain, and premium white live DOM typography carries every essential word. This is an Experience surface: the film carries the atmosphere; the interface provides readable chapters and clear onward routes.

This document is a scoped extraction of the implemented hero on `codex/cinematic-film-hero`, not a replacement for the root `DESIGN.md` or `PRODUCT.md`. It applies only to the film, its curtain layer, overlays, timeline, ending index, static reader, and the navbar's hero-only hide/reveal rule. The navbar's own design and every following section remain outside its authority. The North Star names the already chosen film-led treatment; it adds no new visual direction.
keyCharacteristics: Artwork first: the introduction waits behind an interactive curtain of gold bead strands.
Supplied CGI film, with essential identity and chapter copy rendered as live DOM text.
White Geist typography, a single thin streaming-style timeline, and local dark contrast layers.
Decoded-frame chapter cues over a deliberately slower, user-authorized scroll travel, with artwork-only intervals.
No site navbar inside the film; it reveals as Collections enters.
Full landscape framing on mobile and an equivalent motion-free reading path.

rules.name: The Live White Type Rule
rules.body: Essential hero copy stays live and legible; the film's generated lettering and the curtain never substitute for identity, chapter text or navigation.

rules.name: The Pacing Rule
rules.body: The 1320/1140/950vh travel and the HERO_PACING curve are user-authorized motion settings. Keep them and the Lenis settings unless the user asks for a pacing change; layout refinement does not authorize retiming the film.

dos: Do preserve the supplied film's order and timing, and keep it framed as AI-generated artwork without documentary claims.
Do keep Gwee Per Ming, Ming Creatives and essential chapter copy in readable live DOM text.
Do preserve the authorized 1320/1140/950vh travel, the HERO_PACING curve and the shared scroll owner when refining this hero.
Do keep scrolling as the non-pointer way to open the curtain, and reset the reveal whenever the layer remounts.
Do retain full landscape framing above the mobile reading area and verify chapter/control clearance, including landscape phones.
Do preserve inert hidden chapters, visible keyboard focus and the complete static reader.
Do treat the implementation review as recorded emulated evidence and actual-phone review as still pending.
donts: Don't overwrite the root design system or extend these hero-local rules to unrelated sections.
Don't crop the mobile film into portrait, change the supplied character, or add unrequested film edits.
Don't replace live text with generated glass lettering or describe the imagined scene as documentary proof.
Don't retime captions with wall-clock animation, change the stage height as a spacing optimization, or make curtain interaction mandatory.
Don't reintroduce the corner captions, curtain button, chapter-pill menu, top progress line or always-visible timeline labels, or show the navbar inside the film.
Don't darken the curtain source or the opened room; the closed curtain should match the film.
Don't invent achievements, private data, new identity claims or whole-site component rules.
